result.what_is_wrong: Aggregate parity metrics (Disparate Impact = 0.9791, Demographic Parity Diff = -0.0167) place age_group in the LOW severity band per the provided thresholds. Nevertheless, the per-group breakdown reveals a consistent pattern: seniors have a lower base_rate (0.6716), a lower selection_rate (0.7433) and a lower TPR (0.8764) than mid (selection_rate 0.7995, TPR 0.9151) and young (selection_rate 0.8372, TPR 0.9488). The Theil index (0.296) also indicates residual distributional inequality. In short, overall DI is near parity but seniors are systematically under-selected and have worse true-positive coverage.
result.why_is_wrong: The most plausible mechanisms consistent with the reported numbers are (1) label bias / historical underwriting: seniors exhibit a lower base rate in the data (0.6716) which can encode historical decisions into the labels and suppress selection for that group; and (2) proxying by age-correlated features (e.g., employment status, retirement indicators, income patterns) that allow the model to learn age effects without using the age_group feature directly. These mechanisms produce modest but systematic gaps in selection_rate and TPR even when aggregate DI is close to 1, because DI and DP focus on selection rates while error-rate metrics (TPR/FPR) expose different harms.
result.how_to_fix: Start with a preprocessing remediation: apply AIF360 Reweighing to compute group×label weights that compensate for the lower base_rate for seniors, retrain the model using those weights, and re-evaluate the specified metrics (DI, DP diff, EOD, AOD, Theil) and per-group TPRs. If feature proxies are identified, use AIF360 DisparateImpactRemover or targeted feature engineering/removal to reduce age-correlated signals. If post-training control of error rates is required (to narrow the TPR gap), apply an equalized-odds style method: either AIF360 EqOddsPostprocessing / CalibratedEqOddsPostprocessing or Fairlearn ExponentiatedGradient (or Fairlearn ThresholdOptimizer) with an EqualizedOdds constraint to directly optimize group TPR/FPR tradeoffs. Iterate: compare overall accuracy and fairness tradeoffs, run stakeholder/legal review for acceptable interventions, and add ongoing monitoring of DI and per-group TPR/FPR (and Theil) in production.
